text:
ana: flagging an interesting tail pattern from yesterday's coalesce tuning experiment. small requests (<=8 tokens) are seeing intermittent 20-50ms extra wait.

charlie: saw that in dashboards. p95 stable, p99 has spikes. not constant.

naveen: upload from sim harness shows that when a large request hits the window it creates a long join-chain that tiny reqs inherit. snippet from sim: 
```
step 1: tiny_req enters, waits for slot
step 2: large_req prefetched into same window -> extends window by 12ms
step 3: tiny_req joins, effective wait=12ms
```

lee: sounds like a slot-ownership/lease problem. we currently treat all joins equally which means size-heterogeneous interference is allowed.

ana: (typo) ana: idea: introduce a lightweight "slot auction" where incoming requests bid based on latency_priority and token_cost. tiny requests get higher latency_priority so they win small-fill slots.

charlie: auction sounds neat but increases admission complexity and requires accurate priority signals from API. can we approximate with soft_priority credits?

naveen: simbed both approaches. auction reduced tiny p99 by 35% but increased median for midsize by ~2ms. credits approach reduced tiny p99 by 20% w/ near-zero median impact.

ops-bot: sim-bot: simulation run id=sim-2026-03-22-17 result: auction vs credits comparison uploaded to /sim/results/slot-strategies.csv

ana: another axis: we can add lease_jitter to prevent one large request always holding the coalesce window boundary. small randomized offsets reduce pathological alignment.

lee: lease_jitter is low-risk, we should canary it. combine credits + jitter maybe?

charlie: one operational concern: credits require a replenishment policy. do we tie it to token spend or time? token-spend works but punishes bursty tiny traffic if tenant exhausted. time-based refill is simpler.

naveen: suggested policy in sim: credits_per_shard=64, refill_rate=8/s, carryover=false. that gave good fairness for multi-tenant traces.

ana: what about KV-cache interactions? credits letting tiny reqs win may change access patterns and warmup. we need to correlate eviction_rate with slot allocation changes.

lee: agree. add metrics: slot_wins_by_priority, eviction_delta_on_policy_change, join_latency_by_size_bucket. can someone take metrics?

charlie: i'll open a metrics PR and a dashboard. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/pull/318 (WIP).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: note that we have a running canary path labeled batcher-shard-canary ready for experiments.

ana: proposed rollout plan: 1) canary credits+lease_jitter on a small shard 2) observe p50/p95/p99 and eviction deltas for 24h 3) if tiny p99 improves and eviction delta < 5%, roll to more shards 4) if midsize median regresses >10ms abort.

naveen: i'll run the sim harness with production traces again to stress-test corner cases (hot tenants, bursty API). aim to have data tomorrow.

charlie: action items: charlie -> metrics PR, naveen -> sim runs, ana -> implement credits prototype (small codepath in admission), lee -> coordinate canary deploy.

ana: naming nit: call the feature "soft-priority credits" in configs and UI. avoids "auction" semantics in docs.

lee: good call. i'll add a short RFC blob summarizing tradeoffs and the canary plan.

ana: thanks all. keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the experiment. please post sim links and dashboard links here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: monitor-bot: scheduled canary window: 2026-03-23 01:00 UTC - 2026-03-24 01:00 UTC. automated alerts configured for p99 regressions.
